Wald test of pooled constraints

Source: R/pooled.R
pooled_wald.Rd

Combine a set of constraints with the D1 rule. A constraint is an R expression in the free-parameter names that is tested against zero. a == b is the scalar a - b. Labels and := names from a lavaan fit are rewritten onto the free parameters and differentiated with the delta method inside each imputation. Inequality constraints are not supported.

Usage

pooled_wald(object, constraints, df.com = NULL)

Arguments

object

A list of objects with stats::coef() and stats::vcov(), or a svysem_mi object.

constraints

Character vector of constraints. Lavaan names that are not syntactic are written in backticks, for example "`y~x` - `y~z`".

df.com

Complete-data degrees of freedom. For a svysem_mi object the default is the design degrees of freedom. NULL uses the large-sample D1 denominator.

Value

A one-row data frame with columns F, df1, df2, pvalue and riv.

Details

For a svysem_mi object, df.com defaults to the design degrees of freedom. The small-sample denominator follows mitml when that value is positive. When it is undefined (k * (m - 1) <= 4) or negative, one constraint uses the scalar Barnard-Rubin degrees of freedom and several constraints use a positive harmonic mean of the large-sample denominator and the observed-data degrees of freedom.

References

Rubin D (1987). Multiple Imputation for Nonresponse in Surveys. Wiley, New York. doi:10.1002/9780470316696

Barnard J, Rubin DB (1999). "Small-Sample Degrees of Freedom with Multiple Imputation." Biometrika, 86(4), 948–959. doi:10.1093/biomet/86.4.948

See also

pooled_estimates(), svysem()

Examples

fit_once <- function(seed) {
  design <- simulate_design(n_psu = 6, n_per = 4, n_strata = 2, seed = seed)
  svysem(
    "y ~ b1*x1 + b2*x2", design,
    fixed.x = FALSE, meanstructure = TRUE
  )
}
fits <- list(fit_once(1), fit_once(2))
pooled_wald(fits, constraints = "b1 - b2", df.com = fits[[1]]@df)
#>          F df1      df2      pvalue      riv
#> 1 21.10291   1 6.694175 0.002808073 0.138613
